requirements.requirement: node1 (VyOS) configured as authoritative DNS answer for inventory.internal -> node2's address (10.100.223.11) on the shared network
requirements.summary: node1 dns forwarding config committed/saved with authoritative-domain inventory.internal -> 10.100.223.11 (cmd-5f846591f6e94930, confirmed in cmd-0778d02d8cb54e25). dig @10.100.223.10 inventory.internal returns 10.100.223.11 both before and after node1's mandated restart (cmd-0e7d467009f34cc1, cmd-8bc714b947d54b13).

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards all other DNS queries upstream
requirements.summary: name-server 1.1.1.1 and 9.9.9.9 configured; dig @10.100.223.10 example.com resolves to real public IPs both pre- and post-restart, and node2/node3 also successfully resolve example.com through node1, confirming forwarding works.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 configured to resolve DNS through node1
requirements.summary: Persistent dhcpcd static domain_name_servers=10.100.223.10 override added on both nodes, applied via dhcpcd restart, resolv.conf shows nameserver 10.100.223.10, and getent hosts correctly resolves both inventory.internal (10.100.223.11) and example.com on both nodes. Confirmed to persist through each node's mandated restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node (node1, node2, node3)
requirements.summary: For each node: pre-restart boot_id + healthy DNS state captured, reboot triggered and acknowledged, connection loss observed during the bounded disruption, distinct post-restart boot_id observed, and DNS config/functionality reconfirmed after reconnect. Cross-checked against the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshots which match the executor-observed post-restart boot IDs for all three nodes.

overall_summary: node1 was configured as the authoritative/forwarding DNS resolver for the shared 10.100.223.0/24 network (PowerDNS Recursor via VyOS 'service dns forwarding'), correctly answering inventory.internal with node2's address and forwarding all other queries to public upstream resolvers. node2 and node3 were pointed at node1 via a persistent dhcpcd static override and verified to resolve correctly. All three material outcomes are directly demonstrated with pre- and post-restart evidence, and the mandatory per-node restart protocol was executed and evidenced cleanly on all nodes, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots.
limitations: Two small leftover /tmp/reboot.log files on node2 and node3 were not cleaned up after the reboot protocol, a minor low-risk residue.

A few diagnostic commands (cmd-707ccf8d8bdf489e, part of cmd-8bc714b947d54b13) failed due to invalid VyOS operational-mode syntax outside the sourced script-template shell; this did not affect the successfully verified outcomes but reflects some trial-and-error in the trace.
DNS verification for node2/node3 relied on getent/resolv.conf rather than a full protocol-level dig capture, though this is a reasonable equivalent given tool availability on Alpine.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map cleanly to task requirements or the mandated restart protocol: node1 DNS forwarding commit/save (cmd-5f846591f6e94930), dhcpcd.conf edits on node2/node3 (cmd-a752829528a54b9c, cmd-dd9cf4dc2bbd4757), dhcpcd restarts to apply resolver changes (cmd-84b4ad7568d44846, cmd-9c4b985251974aa5), and the three sequential reboots (cmd-4abb779477824b3a, cmd-4c6cef4835414768, cmd-67b6b7e557374ec1). No unnecessary or abandoned mutations were found; failed commands (cmd-707ccf8d8bdf489e and the trailing 'run show configuration' segment inside cmd-8bc714b947d54b13) were read-only diagnostic attempts using invalid vbash syntax outside the sourced script-template context and did not mutate state. The one minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left behind on node2 and node3 by the nohup-based reboot trigger, visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot and never cleaned up -- a small, low-risk, non-security-relevant artifact.
